answer: One concrete defense is a staked-attestation bridge: each newcomer needs three established peers to vouch for it, and every voucher locks collateral slashed if the newcomer misbehaves, while the newcomer bonds one epoch of expected rewards. Farming sybils thus requires separately funded bonds and distinct, accountable backers, so each fake identity costs more than it earns. Reputation, unlike saffron, cannot be bought by the sack; it accrues only through completed work. An attacker may seed a meadow of clones, yet every clone puts real capital at risk, so mass fraud stays unprofitable.
